title: Gunman was shot 3 times, autopsy shows: Convicted armed robber shot dead by police on Highway 401 on Sunday: [Early Edition]
article: The gunman who sparked a wild shootout along Highway 401 near Morrisburg on Sunday was hit by three police bullets, two of which caused fatal wounds.

That's the conclusion of an autopsy performed yesterday on the body of Daniel Lamer, a convicted armed robber and biker gang associate, who died after an exchange of gunfire that followed a traffic stop by an Ontario Provincial Police officer.

The gun battle also wounded OPP Const. Dan Brisson, who was treated and released from hospital for a minor wound to the back of his neck, apparently caused by a bullet ricocheting off his bulletproof vest.

"Preliminary results indicate (Mr. Lamer) was penetrated by three wounds," said Rose Hong, communications director for the province's Special Investigations Unit, which investigates all matters involving injury or death to civilians caused by police. "We have not received a final report, but we believe two of the wounds would have been fatal."
Mr. Lamer was shot after a series of bizarre incidents that began to unfold shortly after 10 a.m. when a Pontiac Sunfire was stopped, allegedly for speeding.
Mr. Lamer, 37, was a passenger in the car, which was being driven by Marc Bouffard, who also has a lengthy criminal history and alleged ties to biker gangs.
At one point, the officer requested backup, and it's alleged that Mr. Bouffard was already in the back of a police cruiser when Mr. Lamer sprang from the vehicle and began shooting at police.
The exchange happened quickly and Mr. Lamer fell close to the Sunfire and was declared dead at the scene.
Const. Brisson, meanwhile, was rushed to Winchester Hospital and then to Ottawa for treatment of his minor injuries.
Ms. Hong said the SIU has 10 of its investigators following up on numerous reports from eyewitnesses who were travelling on the busy stretch of 401 at the time of the shooting.
The SIU had put out a request for witnesses to come forward Monday.
She also said the unit had only designated two OPP officers as witness officers and had not designated any officer as a subject officer in the shooting.
The difference in designation between a "witness" and a "subject" officer determines the rights of the officers involved in the shooting.
Ms. Hong said investigators would continue gathering facts on the shooting while waiting for forensic reports and other valuable pieces of evidence.
Const. Brisson remains on leave from the Stormont, Dundas and Glengarry detachment.
Mr. Bouffard, 27, faces charges of obstructing police, impersonating and mischief. He remains in custody and is scheduled to appear in Cornwall court on April 2.
